items: PTSD was first introduced into psychiatric classification in DSM-III in 1980 (Dulcan p.345).
DSM-5 and DSM-5-TR moved PTSD from anxiety disorders to Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorders (DSM p.295, Dulcan p.350).
The DSM-IV requirement A2 of responding with intense fear, helplessness, or horror was removed in DSM-5 (Dulcan p.350).
ICD-11 established Complex PTSD (C-PTSD) as a separate diagnosis featuring emotional dysregulation and negative self-concept (Dulcan p.352).
key_numbers: 1 month - minimum duration of symptoms for PTSD diagnosis
6 months - minimum onset delay for delayed expression specifier

items: Hyperactivity of the amygdala drives fear conditioning, hyperarousal, and traumatic flashbacks (StahlNeuro p.362, p.371).
Hypoactivity of vmPFC and ACC causes failure of top-down inhibition over the amygdala (StahlNeuro p.371).
Hippocampal structural and functional deficits impair contextual memory processing (StahlNeuro p.362, Dulcan p.511).
Locus Coeruleus hyperactivity releases excessive Norepinephrine, activating post-synaptic alpha-1 and beta-1 receptors (StahlNeuro p.368-370).
HPA axis dysregulation alters cortisol regulation and stress response in the developing brain (Dulcan p.511).
key_numbers: 4 core symptom clusters in DSM-5-TR (B: Intrusion, C: Avoidance, D: Cognition/Mood, E: Arousal)
2 diagnostic specifiers (With dissociative symptoms, With delayed expression)

items: TF-CBT uses the 8-component PRACTICE model: Psychoeducation, Relaxation, Affective modulation, Cognitive processing, Trauma narrative, In vivo mastery, Conjoint sessions, Enhancing safety (Dulcan p.357).
Prolonged Exposure (PE) uses in vivo and imaginal exposure to drive fear extinction (StahlNeuro p.373, Dulcan p.357).
EMDR combines bilateral stimulation (eye movements, taps) with trauma memory reprocessing (Dulcan p.358-359).
CBITS adapts PRACTICE components for school-based group therapy without direct parent involvement (Dulcan p.358).
Child-Parent Psychotherapy (CPP) targets attachment and dyadic processing in children 0-6 years (Dulcan p.358).
key_numbers: 8 components in the PRACTICE model of TF-CBT
3 to 18 years - age range validated in TF-CBT trials
0 to 6 years - target age range for CPP

items: TF-CBT is validated by over 23 RCTs in more than 2,000 children aged 3-18 years (Dulcan p.357).
EMDR demonstrated equal efficacy to TF-CBT for core PTSD symptoms in a pilot RCT, but TF-CBT was superior for comorbid depression and behavior problems (Diehle et al. 2015, Dulcan p.358-359).
RCT by Cohen et al. (2007) proved adding Sertraline to TF-CBT provides no additional benefit over TF-CBT plus placebo (Dulcan p.359, p.530).
RCT of D-cycloserine (DCS) augmentation of CBT failed to demonstrate superiority over placebo for PTSD symptoms (Scheeringa & Weems 2014, Dulcan p.360).
Medication monotherapy (including SSRIs) has failed to demonstrate efficacy in pediatric PTSD RCTs (Dulcan p.359).
key_numbers: 23 RCTs supporting TF-CBT in children and adolescents
0 added benefit of Sertraline + TF-CBT over TF-CBT alone in Cohen 2007 RCT

items: Trauma-focused psychotherapy (TF-CBT, PE, EMDR) is first-line treatment for all pediatric PTSD (Dulcan p.356, p.360).
Pharmacotherapy is indicated only for severe comorbidities (MDD, ADHD), extreme dangerousness, or severe sleep impairment (Dulcan p.356, p.530).
Benzodiazepines are contraindicated in PTSD because they impair fear extinction learning and risk dependence/disinhibition (StahlNeuro p.381, Dulcan p.359).
Unproven techniques like rebirthing, binding, or nutritional restriction are strictly prohibited due to fatal risks (Dulcan p.360).
Sertraline and Paroxetine are FDA-approved for PTSD in adults, but all SSRIs are off-label for pediatric PTSD (StahlKids p.315, p.380, p.437, Dulcan p.359).
SSRIs block SERT, causing desensitization of 5-HT1A receptors in amygdala and CSTC circuits (StahlNeuro p.365).
Sertraline starting dose in children: 12.5-25 mg/day, adolescents: 25-50 mg/day, target: 50-200 mg/day (Dulcan p.380, StahlKids p.437).
Paroxetine starting dose: 10 mg/day, target: 10-40 mg/day; short half-life requires slow taper to avoid discontinuation syndrome (Dulcan p.380, StahlKids p.380).
FDA Black Box Warning applies to all SSRIs for increased risk of suicidal ideation and behavior in youth (Dulcan p.563, StahlKids p.208).
key_numbers: 2 FDA-approved SSRIs for adult PTSD (Sertraline, Paroxetine)
12.5 to 25 mg/day - initial Sertraline dose in children
50 to 200 mg/day - target Sertraline dose range

items: Prazosin is a competitive alpha-1 adrenergic receptor antagonist that crosses the BBB (StahlNeuro p.339, p.368-370).
Blocks postsynaptic alpha-1 receptors in amygdala to suppress Locus Coeruleus NE-driven nightmares (StahlNeuro p.368-370, Dulcan p.359).
Prazosin starting dose in youth: 0.5-1 mg at bedtime, titrated by 1 mg every 1-2 weeks to target 1-5 mg at bedtime (Dulcan p.359, StahlKids p.437).
First-dose effect / Orthostatic Hypotension requires taking Prazosin at bedtime and monitoring sitting/standing blood pressure (StahlNeuro p.339, StahlKids p.139).
Clonidine (alpha-2 agonist) is an alternative off-label option to reduce hyperarousal and sleep latency (Dulcan p.359, StahlKids p.139).
key_numbers: 0.5 to 1 mg - starting Prazosin dose at bedtime in children
1 to 5 mg - target Prazosin bedtime dose range
1 to 2 weeks - titration interval for Prazosin

high_yield: TF-CBT is the undisputed first-line treatment for pediatric PTSD; pharmacotherapy should not precede trauma-focused psychotherapy (Dulcan p.356, p.360).
Sertraline added to TF-CBT showed zero efficacy advantage over TF-CBT plus placebo in pediatric RCTs (Cohen et al. 2007, Dulcan p.359, p.530).
Benzodiazepines are strictly contraindicated in PTSD because they impair fear extinction learning and increase disinhibition (StahlNeuro p.381, Dulcan p.359).

Prazosin acts as a post-synaptic alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist in the amygdala to suppress trauma nightmares driven by nocturnal Locus Coeruleus NE hyperactivation (StahlNeuro p.368-370, Dulcan p.359).
First-dose orthostatic hypotension (syncope) is the key safety concern with Prazosin; measure sitting/standing BP and administer right before bed (StahlNeuro p.339, StahlKids p.139).
In children under 6 years, PTSD diagnosis requires only 1 symptom from Avoidance/Cognitive-Mood cluster, and intrusion often presents as play reenactment (DSM p.303, Dulcan p.347).
Symptom duration must exceed 1 month for PTSD; symptoms lasting 3 days to 1 month are diagnosed as Acute Stress Disorder (DSM p.302, p.315).
DSM-5-TR includes two specifiers for PTSD: With dissociative symptoms (depersonalization/derealization) and With delayed expression (onset >= 6 months post-trauma) (DSM p.303).
